correctness.rationale: Every candidate host induces an ordered Hamiltonian path through the 32 equal-length mandatory powers, and maximal overlap is never longer than a given occurrence gap. If two roots are conjugate, their transition cost is the least positive shift and independent of exponent. Otherwise it is at least 5p-4, with exponent slope five. Any order with at least eight cross-class transitions therefore costs at least 45p-9 > 40p+2 for p>=3. The sole remaining block-class case is exhaustively minimized at p=3 by local permutations (up to 5! each) and all 4096 subset/end states, giving exactly 122 and an explicit checked host. Its cost increases by exactly 40 per exponent increment; an order with more transitions remains strictly too long. The included verifier reconstructs all data and the local/global DP directly, checks the witness, and compares smaller orders with an independently written unrestricted recurrence. No finite sample is substituted for the all-exponent argument.

value.rationale: This closes a natural, literature-motivated exact shortest-power-superstring gap for infinitely many integer powers at a fixed nontrivial root length, yields a reproducible sharp cubic base 122, and proves a structural rigidity principle for every optimum. The exact length and structure are not automatic consequences of the known upper construction, and the problem is a standard full-family extremal covering invariant rather than an arbitrarily selected computation.
